chunks: [Preparation for the Day of Judgement] And know that you have to pass over the path way (of ṣirāṭ) where steps waver, feet slip away and there are fearful dangers at every step.

O creatures of Allāh, fear Allāh, like the fearing of wise man whom the thought (of next world) has turned away from other matters, fear (of Allāh) has afflicted his body with trouble and pain, his engagement in the night prayer has turned even his short sleep into awakening, hope (of eternal recompense) keeps him thirsty in the day, abstention has curbed his desires, and remembrance of Allāh is ever moving his tongue. He entertains fear before dangers. He avoids uneven ways in favour of clear ones. He follows the shortest route to secure his purpose

wishfulness does not twist his thinking and ambiguities do not blind his eyes. He enjoys deep sleep and passes his day happily because of the happiness of good tidings and pleasure of (eternal bounties).

key_terms.الزُّهْد: Asceticism or detachment from worldly desires
key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The path over Hellfire on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: How should a believer cultivate true God-consciousness (Taqwa) to navigate the trials of the afterlife?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Al-Gharra*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defines true piety (*Taqwa*) not merely as fear, but as a holistic state where intellectual contemplation (*Tafakkur*) and physical devotion (*Tahajjud*) converge to secure safe passage across the *Sirat*. This exhortation highlights the Shia emphasis on the integration of inner spiritual awareness with outward ritual practice as the means to navigate the eschatological trials of the Bridge to Paradise. The description of the believer as one whose heart is occupied by thought and body by fear underscores the dynamic balance between hope (*Raja'*) and awe (*Khawf*) essential for spiritual stability.
